303A.5 / CHAPTER 5 OF 11

Harvest & residual exposure

After the move, how much risk should remain?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Choose the container02Opportunity vs portfolio risk03Scout, then earn promotion04Adding up or down05Harvest & residual exposure06Reset the mission07Break the attachment08Attention & holding time09Match the evidence to the market10Portfolio limits & concentration11Measure the net result

01Definition

Harvesting realizes part or all of a position. A runner is deliberately retained exposure with its own limits.

02Why it matters

A chart gain is not realized capital until a sale executes.

03What to check

  • Actual proceeds after execution costs
  • Remaining position value and exit capacity
  • Why any retained exposure still belongs in the plan

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

A partial sale reduces exposure and the remainder has clear conditions.

Dangerous

Leftover inventory becomes an indefinite hold without reassessment.

05Beginner mistake

Calling the remainder risk-free after recovering the initial spend.

06Takeaway

A runner is still capital at risk.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    A trader buys 100 units for $100, ignoring costs.

  2. 02

    Selling 50 units for $150 realizes $100 profit on their $50 cost basis.

  3. 03

    The remaining 50 units still have value that can be lost.

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

You invest $200 and later receive $220 net from partial sales. Original cash has been recovered, but a remaining position marked at $300 can still lose $300 of current value. “House money” hides that economic exposure.

How to investigate it

Record actual sale proceeds after fees, remaining units, current conservative valuation, and executable sale quotes. Reconcile realized cash against original cost. Decide why the residual deserves its present size; do not use recovered cost as proof that holding has no risk.

Check your reasoning — answered

After recovering cost, does a $300 residual have zero downside? It has no unrecovered original cash under that accounting, but it still has $300 of present marked exposure that may fall or be difficult to realize.

Trace it externally

Use actual fills, costs, remaining inventory, and current sell quotes. Meme Fast does not execute harvesting or reconcile your realized profit.

Go deeper

Choose full exit, partial reduction, or residual exposure using current evidence and the plan. Recovering original capital is a cash-flow milestone, not the realized-profit calculation. Cost basis methods and taxes depend on applicable accounting rules; this example uses one purchase lot and excludes costs.
